The mood conveyed in the text is one of humid, sensory-rich nostalgia and carefree tranquility. The atmosphere is heavy and slow, emphasized by the "hot and heavy" heat and the constant "drone of cicadas," which creates a sense of stillness and immersion in the moment. This atmosphere contributes to the narrative by establishing a strong sense of place and time, evoking a feeling of simplicity and innocence associated with childhood summers. The juxtaposition of the oppressive heat with the "carefree joy" of children playing highlights a bittersweet or idealized memory, drawing the reader into a reflective state.

Regarding the specific question embedded in the text: The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.
